issues.description: The problem text explicitly instructs students to use StringBuilder for Animal.name, but the UML in the problem statement lists the name attribute as type String and the provided solution implements Animal.name as a String. This mismatch between textual instruction, UML, and solution creates confusion about the intended attribute type (and therefore constructor/getter/setter signatures) and may cause students to implement the wrong type or fail tests that expect a different type.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent. Either (A) update the problem UML and textual instructions to require a String name (and remove the recommendation to use StringBuilder), or (B) change the solution and any templates to use a StringBuilder name field and update constructors, getter and setter signatures accordingly (e.g., private StringBuilder name; public Animal(StringBuilder name) / public StringBuilder getName() / public void setName(StringBuilder name)). Prefer option B only if tests and learning goals explicitly require showing use of StringBuilder; otherwise prefer option A to match the current solution.
